messages:
incident-bot: P1 alert — sudden spike in 429s across hosted-api (region: us-east-1). Estimated affected customers: ~30 (mostly high-burst plans). Paging oncall.
marie: acked. I'm paged. seeing the noise in dashboards. tagging @sre-james and @ops-ella
sre-james: on it. initial glance: token counters per-tenant jumped, throttler service throughput dropped by ~60% at 09:12 UTC. throwing 429s for short bursts.
ops-ella: seeing 429 flood in logs: `GET /v1/generate 429 x2000 09:12->09:25`. can we throttle less aggressively for bursts? looks like new policy rollout went live ~09:10
marie: confirmed — config service shows a rollout of `burst_throttle_v2` at 09:09 via deploy-bot. canary was supposed to be 5% but flags show 100% due to a rollout selector bug.
deploy-bot: Deployment event: config/burst_throttle_v2 promoted -> stage=prod by eng-release-bot at 2026-03-15T09:09:11Z (id: cfg-5587)
stella: omg, that selector bug is the one we saw in staging last month. it ignores the tag when the override key is missing.
sre-james: mitigation suggestion: flip the kill-switch for the feature flag or rollback config. which is faster?
marie: kill-switch via feature-flag service should be faster. ops-ella, can you flip the flag and limit to canary groups only?
ops-ella: doing a quick dry-run. running:
```
# curl to set flag
curl -X POST "https://flags.redwood.internal/v1/flags/burst_throttle_v2/toggle" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"state":"off","reason":"emergency rollback - overthrottle"}'
```
ops-ella: sent. feature-flag service responded 200 -> flag state: OFF for prod.
marie: observing metrics... 429 rate falling. latency normalizing. thank you. keep watch for config re-promotes.
sre-james: adding emergency exemption for enterprise-tier customers so billing and SSO-heavy tenants are unaffected while we fully roll back. patching bypass list now.
stella: command to patch bypass (internal db):
```
UPDATE throttles.exempt_tenants
SET active = true
WHERE tenant_tag = 'enterprise' AND active = false;
```
stella: ran that as read-only then applied. DB change committed at 09:22 UTC.
oncall-nick: saw a flapping behavior — some requests still 429 because edge caches had old policy. purging relevant caches `edge-config-cache:burst_throttle_v2`.
eng-release-bot: rollback initiated: config service reverted cfg-5587 -> cfg-5531 at 09:25 UTC
deploy-bot: Rollback success: `burst_throttle_v2` removed from prod. rollbacks trace id: rb-2026-03-15-09-25
marie: confirm final state: throttler service config = v1, exemptions include enterprise, 429 rate back to baseline. any residual customer impact observed?
sre-james: we still have a handful of customers who hit client-side retry storms due to earlier 429s. support queue trending up. marking customers with active incidents.
ops-ella: temp mitigation: enable increased retry-backoff header instructing SDKs to wait (via edge response header): `Retry-After: 3s` for 15m window
stella: created a short status page update draft. want to be transparent: 'partial degradation due to throttling policy deploy, now mitigated; impacted customers may see transient errors 09:12-09:30 UTC.'
marie: handoff: I'm going offline in 30m. @oncall-nick please take the overnight watcher. leave a runbook note and postmortem owner.
oncall-nick: taking handoff. will monitor error budget and support tickets. assigned postmortem to @stella. timeline notes added to runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/burst-throttle-incident
sre-james: preliminary root-cause: rollout selector logic ignored override keys when feature flag payload lacked `selector_version`. leads to full-prod target instead of canary. also a missing guard in config-service tests.
stella: postmortem checklist items: incident timeline, reproducer, tests to add, customer outreach, and gating for future rollouts. assigning SLA-impact calc to finance later.
marie: customer-impact assessment: roughly 30 mid/large tenants saw elevated 429s, 7 customers filed support tickets, estimated 2% of requests lost in 13-minute window. we'll confirm exact numbers in postmortem.
ops-ella: follow-ups:
- add integration test for selector_version absent case
- require manual approval for config promotion until auto-rollout is patched
- add automated smoke check post-config-promotion to detect global jump in throttles
sre-james: will open blocker PR for throttler: add safe-fail to prefer old policy if selector mismatch. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/throttler/pull/782
stella: postmortem owner: @stella
eng-release-bot: scheduled job: block auto-promote for config/burst_throttle_v2 until PR-782 merged
marie: thanks team. good mitigation. please keep updates in this thread with any customer escalations. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident P1 -> mitigated. transitioning to post-incident review state. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1779401234
